Module notify chain storage and broadcast context.
Locked console removal internals and list structure.
Architecture debug init and exit behaviour.
Module load notifier payload and event codes.

Driver read and init and teardown contracts beyond observed use.

findings.text: Module layer exposes registration for load and unload listeners. Caller supplies a notifier object that the core appends to a shared blocking chain for later broadcast.
Module layer exposes removal of a previously registered load and unload listener. Caller supplies the same notifier object for detachment from the shared blocking chain.

Console layer exposes removal of a previously registered console. The public entry guards the operation with the console list lock and delegates to an internal locked removal routine before returning its status.

Debug core exposes installation of the current remote input output driver. It enforces a single occupant slot and publishes a newcomer only after successful preparation while preserving the incumbent on failure.
Debug core exposes removal of the current remote input output driver. It disarms shared services and clears the occupant slot before optional teardown of the removed driver.

Debug core exposes single character input from the current driver. A no data marker becomes negative one and in keyboard debugger mode value one hundred twenty seven becomes eight while other values pass through.

Shared debug callbacks for module events and reboot and console are armed at most once under control of a registered marker and disarmed symmetrically. Repeated arm or disarm while already in the desired state has no effect.

Replacement and publication of the current driver pointer is serialised by a dedicated registration guard held across inspection and update. Teardown of the prior driver and arming of shared services occur outside the guarded region.
Changes to console list membership during removal are serialised by holding the console list guard across the entire operation.

Per exception state groups trap identity plus processor identity plus forwarding choice plus thread selection plus saved register reference plus readiness reference. Trap identity uses vector plus signal plus error code and thread selection uses two unsigned handles plus a signed selector.

Per processor debugger record groups opaque debugger data plus task reference plus exception progress plus return disposition plus interrupt nesting depth plus entry marker plus rounding marker. Progress and disposition and depth and entry use integers while rounding uses a boolean and data uses an untyped pointer.

Driver occupancy moves between empty and occupied. First successful install moves empty to occupied and arms shared services. Later replacement remains occupied with the newcomer published. Removal moves occupied to empty and disarms services.

Breakpoint slots cycle among free and allocated disabled and allocated enabled with an optional delayed step marker. Allocation claims a free slot and publishes enabled by default while later operations toggle enablement or return the slot to free and clear any delayed marker.

Backtrace scope is selected by verb with verb bta for full listings showing active processors before remaining threads and separately verb btp for pid lookup and separately verb btt for raw address and separately verb btc for processor selection and separately plain verb bt for current context. Single task display checks readability and state filter before printing header and stack with optional interactive continuation.
Reboot handling is exposed as a notifier object with maximal ordering priority and no successor so that it runs earliest during reboot processing.

Keyboard debugger exposes breakpoint verbs through a table plus a separate hardware verb. Verbs include bp for setting and separately bl for listing and separately bc for clearing and separately be for enabling and separately bd for disabling and separately ss for stepping plus bph for hardware breaks with usage hints and flow control attributes.

Early boot handling offers a wait option that records a request for the earliest possible breakpoint and performs early keyboard debugger preparation with an immediate breakpoint when input output services are already present on capable builds.
Removal of the input output driver while a remote session remains marked connected triggers a fatal consistency check. Callers must disconnect before teardown.

Replacement over an incumbent that lacks teardown support is rejected as busy without disturbing the current driver. Failure during preparation of the newcomer likewise aborts publication and preserves the prior occupant.

Breakpoint creation rejects missing addresses and architecturally refused addresses and duplicate addresses and table exhaustion and hardware lengths above eight and argument count errors. Display and update paths skip free slots and report absence when no slot matches.
Processor debug role flags use distinct low bits with want master as one and separately next master as two and separately slave as four and separately want backtrace as eight.

Internal debugger event markers use large negative sentinels with pass event as minus twelve thousand three hundred forty five and separately switch processor event as minus one hundred twenty three thousand four hundred fifty six.

Keyboard controller addresses use status port one hundred and separately data port ninety six with output full signalled by bit zero and separately mouse output full by bit five. Control mapping subtracts sixty four.
Fixed capacities use command length two hundred fifty six and separately thread identity text eight and separately maximum thread query seventeen.

Task state display derives one character from scheduler state with idle tasks that are truly quiescent shown as dash and sleeping lockless daemons in lower case. Empty filter excludes dash and separately i and separately m and separately s while letter A matches all and other filters require membership.

Stack display raises a printk trap count across the operation and prefers a per processor dump with verbose console level for the running task of a processor while using generic printing otherwise before restoring level and lowering the trap count.

Remote protocol state keeps paired fixed input and output buffers plus replay markers for prior input plus a register image rounded up to whole words plus a message buffer one larger than the packet maximum.
Keyboard debugger input keeps a prompt string sized to the command limit plus a printk trap counter plus a formatted output processor selector initialised to negative one meaning no override.

Character polling uses a small fixed table whose first entry reads from debug input output and whose remaining entries are empty with a poll index of one and a saved pointer to the current exception state.

Running task test reduces to a scheduler current check and per processor saved task comes from indexed debugger information while single byte accessibility probing is expressed through a sized area reader.

Output staging uses a small fixed buffer with a next write pointer plus available size and grep suspension counters while keyboard handling separately tracks presence and last result in dedicated integers.
Debug core header defines a conventional single inclusion guard macro.

Process status output validates readability before printing address plus identifiers plus processor affinity plus state character plus thread reference plus current marker plus name with warnings for mismatched per processor records. Suppressed summary counts hidden idle and daemon tasks.

Hardware breakpoint kinds are presented through a small label table indexed by numeric kind with out of range yielding empty text. Hardware option parsing accepts mnemonic inst and separately datar and separately dataw with optional length defaulting to one.
Breakpoint clear and enable and disable sub operations are encoded internally as zero and separately one and separately two selected by command name.
